products.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central North Carolina, including the
following counties, Alamance, Chatham, Cumberland, Durham,
Edgecombe, Franklin, Granville, Halifax, Harnett, Johnston, Lee,
Nash, Orange, Person, Sampson, Vance, Wake, Warren, Wayne and
Wilson.

* WHEN...From this afternoon through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A vigorous storm system will combine with anomalous moisture,
instability, and strong lift to produce periods of moderate to
heavy rainfall across the watch area. Rainfall totals of 2 to 5
inches are expected, with locally higher amounts also possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
products.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 1:47AM EST until November 26 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Raleigh NC
products.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

products.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph
expected.

* WHERE...All of central North Carolina.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 10 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
